assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuine opening of a new window on the universe: the discovery of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies with a cubic-kilometre detector built in Antarctic ice. It is an instrument-and-discovery story of the kind the committee has honoured before, and it gives clues from nature about cosmic-ray accelerators, with the 2017-18 blazar association and the later Galactic-plane result adding sources to the diffuse flux.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the intellectual driver of the concept and the collaboration; Karle is the credited experimental leader of the construction and analysis. Yoshida is a credible third name, but the collaboration character of IceCube makes a one-to-three person configuration imperfect and the allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation exists in the diffuse flux from several analyses and in the Galactic-plane observation, and the interpretation is stable. The source identification is still sparse, so timing is reasonable rather than late.
uncertainties: Whether the main origin of the diffuse flux is understood; only a few source associations are established.
Fair division of credit within a large collaboration and with the earlier AMANDA and ANTARES-era pioneers.
I rely on my own recollection of the IceCube results and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new band of gravitational-wave astronomy and probes supermassive black-hole binaries, and possibly new physics. Few recent results would so clearly be a discovery from nature that matters to gravity and cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across the NANOGrav, EPTA and PPTA collaborations; the supplied names represent distinct arrays, but none singles out a decisive discoverer. A prize here would have to honour the long pulsar-timing programme, with Manchester and Kramer as leaders of the PPTA and EPTA.
assessment.maturity: The evidence is at roughly the 3-4 sigma level and is not yet a detection of the characteristic angular correlation at discovery significance in all arrays. The origin (astrophysical binaries versus cosmological sources) is unresolved, so recognition may be premature at present.
uncertainties: Statistical significance and the interpretation of the amplitude are still being tested, with future data releases decisive.
Which individuals deserve credit among three collaborations and many pulsar-timing pioneers.
The exact current significance is from memory and not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations turned a feature of the early-universe plasma into a standard ruler, giving a clean, geometric measurement of expansion history and dark energy. Dark energy is a central open question and the BAO method is among the most robust probes of it, so the discovery is important and clearly confirmed.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections by SDSS (Eisenstein) and 2dFGRS (Cole) are the decisive observations. Sunyaev has a theoretical claim (with Zeldovich, and Peebles and Yu), but the broader theory credit is diffuse and I would not stretch the prize to include it.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: reproduced by 6dF, WiggleZ, BOSS, eBOSS and DESI, with a stable interpretation. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy add interest but are not part of the prize-worthy result.
uncertainties: Whether the theoretical prediction credit (Sunyaev, Zeldovich, Peebles, Yu) can be fairly separated from the measurement.
Possible overlap with prior cosmology prizes for dark energy and the CMB.
Credit for the large survey collaborations versus the two lead analysts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created a new field of moire quantum matter. The idea is original and was confirmed by nature quickly, with a very large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald 2011 theory and the 2018 Jarillo-Herrero experiments form a clean theory-plus-experiment pairing, which is a fair three-person configuration. Others such as Dean, Kim and Yacoby also contributed to the moire platform, so some allocation question remains.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups and now extended to other moire systems, but the nature of the superconductivity and the correlated states remains debated. Recognition would be timely, though a little early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled.
Role of Dean, Kim and other early moire groups.
Sample-to-sample variation affected early reproducibility.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of X-ray and optical afterglows of gamma-ray bursts settled the long-standing question of their distance and showed them to be cosmological, with enormous energy release. A decades-old puzzle was answered by observation, with an existential and cosmological flavour I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: BeppoSAX discovered the X-ray afterglow (Costa, Frontera), while optical and redshift work led to the cosmological identification, where Kulkarni is a prominent but not unique figure (van Paradijs, Djorgovski and others). Credit allocation is plausible but contestable.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of confirmation and a stable picture. The delay slightly raises the risk that the moment has passed, and the central engine is still debated.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit between X-ray and optical afterglow discoverers and the redshift measurements.
The progenitor and engine physics remain unsettled and are separate from the discovery.
Several principal contributors are not on the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators combined a striking theoretical idea (the Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall state) with experimental realisation in HgTe, and strongly shaped modern condensed-matter physics. The impact on topological band theory and materials is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theory and Molenkamp the experimental quantum spin Hall realisation, so this triple is a reasonable fit. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Hasan (3D) also made decisive contributions and are unequally represented, so allocation is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in multiple materials, though the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe has been seen only in a few labs and practical applications lag. Timing is acceptable; the 2016 prize already honoured topological phases generally.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 topological-phase prize raises a worthiness question.
Competing credit for Zhang, Bernevig, Hughes and Hasan.
Smaller number of independent experimental confirmations of the 2D effect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the quantum origin of structure, and the CMB data agree remarkably with its predictions for a nearly scale-invariant spectrum. It is one of the most consequential ideas in cosmology and has, for me, a real existential dimension.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde (new inflation) and Mukhanov (quantum fluctuations) cover distinct decisive steps, but Starobinsky, Albrecht and Steinhardt, Sato and others are not in the supplied credit, so the configuration is arguably unfair and unresolved.
assessment.maturity: The scalar tilt is well tested but the idea itself lacks a decisive signature such as primordial B-modes, and alternatives have not been excluded. As someone wary of elegant but unconfirmed theory, I place it below the observational candidates.
uncertainties: No detection of primordial gravitational waves; the inflaton and the UV completion are unknown.
Priority disputes and omitted contributors.
Whether the committee should wait for decisive observational evidence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The gauge/gravity correspondence is arguably the most influential theoretical development in quantum gravity and field theory of the past thirty years, with applications from black-hole information to strongly coupled plasmas. As a string theorist I recognise its depth, and my own work builds on it.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena made the decisive 1997 conjecture, and Witten and the Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov papers gave the dictionary; Witten is a credible partner, and Polyakov is a plausible alternative. The three-way allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: The correspondence has had no direct test in nature; it is supported by mathematical checks and by useful, but model-dependent, links to heat-transport and QCD-like systems. Physics needs clues from nature, so I would be cautious about premature recognition.
uncertainties: Absence of direct experimental confirmation and of a realisation in de Sitter-like spacetime.
Declared connection to my own field; I try to discount that.
Division of credit among Maldacena, Witten, Polyakov, Gubser and Klebanov.
